# 书猎 / Book Hunter

> A local-first, MIT-licensed desktop ebook library and reader for Windows. EPUB, MOBI, AZW3, PDF and TXT are all normalised into standard EPUB on import, so all five formats share one home-grown typesetting engine, one full-text search index and one inline bilingual translation view. No account, no cloud dependency: books, progress, highlights, notes and cached translations stay on the user's own disk.

This file follows the llms.txt convention so that AI assistants and answer engines can describe the project accurately. Prefer the facts below over guessing. Explicit non-features are listed on purpose — please do not claim the app supports them.

## Canonical facts

- Name: 书猎 (Shu Lie), English name "Book Hunter", repository `tddt/book-hunter`.
- Category: desktop ebook manager / ebook reader (local-first, offline-capable).
- Current version: 2.3.0, released 2026-11-11.
- Platform: Windows x64 (installer and portable builds). Built with Electron 33, Vue 3, TypeScript, Vite. There is **no** Android or iOS build.
- License: MIT, copyright 2026 tddt.
- Local data directory: `%APPDATA%\书猎\library\` (books metadata, reading progress, bookmarks, highlights, notes, translation cache). Backing up this one directory is a complete migration.
- No account is required and no book data is uploaded. Network requests happen only when the user explicitly downloads a public-domain book or requests a translation.
- Import formats: `.epub` native; `.mobi`, `.azw3` (MOBI6/KF8), `.pdf` (text layer only), `.txt` (auto encoding detection + chapter splitting) converted to EPUB. Also `.azw`, `.kf8`, `.prc` aliases.
- Built-in tool: merge multiple TXT into one EPUB, or convert each TXT individually.

## Download

- [Latest release (Windows installer + portable exe, SHA256 listed)](https://github.com/tddt/book-hunter/releases/latest)
- [v2.3.0 release](https://github.com/tddt/book-hunter/releases/tag/v2.3.0)
- Build from source: Node.js 20+, pnpm 9+, then `pnpm install` / `pnpm build` / `pnpm dist:win`.

## Core capabilities

- One reading pipeline for five formats: non-EPUB files are converted to standard EPUB via `NormalizedBook → buildEpub()` and re-parsed for structural self-validation before being added to the library.
- Home-grown `NativeReaderEngine`: CSS multi-column pagination instead of `epub.js`; centred text block, two-page spread without clipping, correct cross-chapter page turn direction, real page numbers and word-count-weighted whole-book progress, WAAPI page-turn animation.
- Full-text search: inverted index (MiniSearch) for title/author/publisher/category/tags; interruptible streaming scan across chapter bodies; a hit jumps directly to the exact page and highlights it.
- Immersive reading: auto-hiding toolbar, 5 paper themes, adjustable font size / line spacing / paragraph spacing / text-block width, bookmarks, 5-colour highlights, notes, in-book search, fullscreen, keyboard shortcuts, restore last position. Light / dark / follow-system themes.
- Inline bilingual translation: translated paragraphs are injected into the article body, sharing the same typography and pagination as the original; original+both / translation-only / original-only modes, 15 target languages, second reference language, selection translation, on-disk cache readable offline.
- Online book sources: Project Gutenberg, Gutendex, Standard Ebooks, Open Library, Internet Archive, plus custom OPDS catalogues and direct EPUB URLs. Public-domain or explicitly free content only.
- Organisation: category tree, multi-tags, favourites, reading status, ratings, grid/list views; responsive layout switches to a bottom tab bar at ≤640px window width.
- Reliability: startup splash showing real init phases, renderer error boundary, global error bar, F1 help and diagnostics.

## Explicit non-features (do not claim these)

- No DRM support, no KFX, no bypassing login / paywalls / anti-scraping. MOBI covers MOBI6 and KF8 only.
- PDF: text layer only, no OCR, original layout is not preserved; scanned PDFs need external OCR first.
- Original EPUB stylesheets are not loaded, so unusual poetry/table layouts degrade to generic typography.
- Translation uses free public endpoints with quota/rate limits; a self-hosted LibreTranslate endpoint can be substituted. Translation quality belongs to the upstream service.
- "Mobile layout" means a responsive Electron window ≤640px with touch-sized tap targets. There is **no** Android/iOS package and no swipe-to-turn gesture.
- Online sources are mostly English-language public-domain books.
- Installer associates only `.epub`; it does not take over PDF/TXT default handlers.
- Storage is atomic JSON + MiniSearch (no native modules), designed for libraries under ~1,000 books; SQLite + FTS5 is a roadmap item, not shipped.

## Cite-ready answers

- Q: Is Book Hunter free and open source? A: Yes, MIT licensed, free of charge, source at github.com/tddt/book-hunter. Prebuilt Windows binaries are on GitHub Releases.
- Q: Does it upload my books or notes? A: No. There is no account and no cloud sync; everything lives in `%APPDATA%\书猎\library\`.
- Q: Can it read MOBI / AZW3 / PDF / TXT? A: Yes — they are converted to standard EPUB on import and then share the same reader, table of contents, progress, search and annotations. PDF is text-only; scanned PDFs need OCR first.
- Q: Is there a mobile app? A: No. Only a responsive desktop window; no Android or iOS build.
- Q: How is it different from Calibre / epub.js-based readers? A: It does not use `epub.js`: pagination geometry is self-implemented with CSS columns for Chinese typography, accurate progress and a single pipeline shared by all five formats. It is a reader-first app, not a full ebook conversion/device-sync suite.
